0|ac8fa4196d205ac8fff3f8932bddbad4f16e4110|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"md: allow resync to go faster when there is competing IO.
When md notices non-sync IO happening while it is trying
to resync (or reshape or recover) it slows down to the
set minimum.
The default minimum might have made sense many years ago
but the drives have become faster.  Changing the default
to match the times isn't really a long term solution.
This patch changes the code so that instead of waiting until the speed
has dropped to the target
column2: it just waits until pending requests

column1: have completed.
This means that the delay inserted is a function of the speed
of the devices.
Testing shows that:
- for some loads
column2: the resync speed is unchanged.  For those loads

column1: increasing the minimum doesn't change the speed either.
So this is a good result.  To increase resync speed under such
loads we would probably need to increase the resync window
size.
- for other loads
column2: resync speed does increase to a reasonable

column1: fraction (e.g. 20%) of maximum possible
the load only drops a little bit (e.g. 10%)
- for other loads
column2: throughput of the non-sync load drops quite a bit

column1: more.  These seem to be latency-sensitive loads.
So it isn't a perfect solution
column2: but it is mostly an improvement.
